script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Comedy
Theme: second chances

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

JAMES (30s, quirky, introverted), sitting alone, furiously types on a laptop. His eyes dart back and forth as he reads his own words on the screen.

Waitress (late 20s, bubbly) approaches with a tray of coffees.

WAITRESS: (cheerfully) Here you go, sir! Decaf for you?

James looks up, startled. He's so engrossed in his work that he didn't hear her coming.

JAMES: (stammering) Uh, yes, please. Thank you.

WAITRESS: (laughing) You're in the zone, aren't you?

James nods, then winces as she sets the coffee down, sloshing some on the table. He looks at her sympathetically.

JAMES: You know, I used to write for a living. But then I made a mistake... and lost everything.

WAITRESS: (smiling) Oh, no! What happened?

INT. JAMES' APARTMENT - FLASHBACK - NIGHT

Young James (20s), sitting on a bed, looking distraught as his girlfriend, LUCY (also 20s), yells at him.

LUCY: (angrily) I can't believe you plagiarized my brother's work!

James looks away, ashamed.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Back in the present, James looks up at the Waitress, his expression thoughtful.

JAMES: I guess I've been given a second chance. And I'm not going to waste it.

WAITRESS: (smiling) That's the spirit! You know, my boss is looking for a new writer. You should apply!

INT. COFFEE SHOP - OFFICE - DAY

James sits nervously across from the COFFEE SHOP OWNER (40s, stern, but fair).

OWNER: (leaning back in his chair) So, you want to write for our coffee shop? Why should I hire you?

James hesitates, then looks the Owner in the eye.

JAMES: Because I've learned from my mistakes. And I'm not going to let them define me anymore.

The Owner nods, impressed.

OWNER: Alright. You have a week to write a sample piece for our new menu. Good luck.

INT. JAMES' APARTMENT - NIGHT

James sits at his laptop, determined. He types furiously, his eyes filled with focus and determination.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

One week later, James walks in with a printed copy of his sample piece in hand. He hands it to the Waitress.

WAITRESS: (excitedly) You did it! Our boss loved it! You're in!

James beams with pride.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Months later, James is now a regular at the coffee shop, and his work is featured prominently on their menus and online presence. Customers compliment him on his clever wordplay and engaging descriptions.

JAMES: (to the Waitress) You know, I owe this place a lot. Thanks for believing in me.

WAITRESS: (smiling) It was my pleasure. And who knows? Maybe one day, you'll be writing screenplays again.

James laughs, considering the idea.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

As James continues to write for the coffee shop, he begins to feel a renewed sense of purpose and passion for his craft. He looks forward to each new day, knowing that he's been given a second chance to prove himself.

FADE OUT.
